note.explanation: Impulse measures the change in an object's momentum when a force acts on it. A force acting for a longer time can produce the same change in momentum with a smaller average force.
examples: A cricketer draws his hands back while catching a ball to increase the time of impact and reduce the force on his hands.
Packing materials increase the time over which a fragile object slows down, reducing the force on it.
note.checkAnswer: Impulse is the total change in momentum of an object when a large force acts on it for a short time.
note.simple: Impulse tells us how much an object's momentum changes during a force. More time for the change means less average force.
note.checkQuestion: What happens to the average force if the same change in momentum takes place over a longer time?
note.title: Momentum and Impulse
steps: Find the object's mass and velocity.
For a force acting over time, use F = Δp/Δt.
For an impact, calculate the change in momentum as final momentum minus initial momentum.
note.answer: Impulse is the total change in momentum of an object when a large force acts on it for a short time.

written.text: Inflatable airbags are installed in the vehicles as safety equipment. In terms of momentum, what is the advantage of airbags over seatbelts?
written.finalAnswer: Airbags increase the time over which a passenger's momentum changes, reducing the force acting on the passenger.

rubric.why: The explanation must identify the momentum change during a collision.
rubric.description: Identify the passenger's momentum change.
rubric.how: State that the passenger's momentum changes during the collision.

rubric.why: The safety advantage comes from increasing the time for that change.
rubric.description: Explain how airbags affect the time interval.
rubric.how: State that airbags increase the time over which momentum changes.

rubric.why: A longer time for the same momentum change means a smaller average force.
rubric.description: Relate the longer time to force.
rubric.how: Use F = Δp/Δt to explain that the average force is reduced.

rubric.why: The answer must connect the advantage to the airbag's protective effect.
rubric.description: State the safety outcome.
rubric.how: Conclude that airbags reduce the force on the passenger.

modelAnswer: During a collision, the passenger's momentum changes.
An airbag increases the time over which this change in momentum occurs.
Since F = Δp/Δt, increasing the time reduces the average force on the passenger.
Thus, airbags reduce the impact force on the passenger.

rubric.why: For the same change in momentum, more time means less average force.
rubric.description: Link the extra time to the average force.
rubric.how: Use F = Δp/Δt to show the force is reduced.

rubric.why: The answer should state the practical benefit to the fielder.
rubric.description: State the effect on the fielder.
rubric.how: Conclude that the force on the hands is smaller.

modelAnswer: The ball's momentum changes when the fielder brings it to rest.
Drawing the hands backward increases the time over which this change takes place.
Since F = Δp/Δt, the average force on the hands is reduced.
This reduces the impact of the ball on the fielder's hands.

written.text: A ball of mass 0.4 kg is dropped on the floor from a height of 1.8 m. The ball rebounds straight upward to a height of 0.8 m. What is the magnitude and direction of the impulse applied to the ball by the floor?

rubric.why: The mass and the two heights determine the ball's velocities.
rubric.description: Record the given values.
rubric.how: Write m = 0.4 kg, drop height = 1.8 m and rebound height = 0.8 m.

rubric.why: The speed before impact and rebound speed must be found from the heights.
rubric.description: Find the speeds before and after impact.
rubric.how: Using g = 10 m s⁻², find the impact speed 6 m s⁻¹ and rebound speed 4 m s⁻¹.

rubric.why: The momenta have opposite directions, so their directions must be accounted for.
rubric.description: Use a consistent direction for the momentum change.
rubric.how: Take upward as positive; initial momentum is downward and final momentum is upward.

rubric.why: Impulse equals the change in momentum.
rubric.description: Calculate the impulse from the momentum change.
rubric.how: Use impulse = 0.4(4 − (−6)) N s.

rubric.why: The answer must give both the magnitude and direction.
rubric.description: State the final impulse.
rubric.how: Give 4 N s upward.

modelAnswer: Speed before hitting the floor = √(2gh) = √(2 × 10 × 1.8) = 6 m s⁻¹
Impulse = change in momentum = m(v_f − v_i)
The impulse applied by the floor is 4 N s, upward.

explain.title: Momentum
explain.body: The momentum of a moving body is the product of its mass and velocity. Therefore, vector p = m × vector v. Momentum is a vector quantity, and its SI unit is kg m s⁻¹, which can also be written as N s.

explain.title: Change in momentum
explain.body: When an object's velocity changes from v_i to v_f, its change in momentum depends on its mass and the velocity change: m(v_f − v_i). Keep the direction signs for the velocities.

explain.title: Impulse
explain.body: When a large force F acts on an object for a short interval of time, the impulse of the force is defined as the total change in momentum of the object. The product F × Δt equals that change in momentum.

explain.title: Force and momentum
explain.body: The rate of change of momentum of a body is equal to the force acting on it. In symbols, F = Δp/Δt. The direction of change in momentum is that of the force.

explain.title: Why longer impact time helps
explain.body: For the same change in momentum, increasing the time reduces the average force. This is why a cricketer draws his hands back and why soft packing materials help protect fragile objects.

mistakes: Forgetting to convert grams to kilograms before calculating momentum or force.
Dropping the negative sign of an initial velocity when the object is moving in the opposite direction.
Using momentum instead of change in momentum in the force equation.
Forgetting that impulse has the same units as momentum: N s or kg m s⁻¹.
Giving an impact answer without stating its direction when the question asks for magnitude and direction.
